To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ELISA method is a promising technique for the diagnosis of primary biliary cirrhotis (PBC), but it must be used in combination with other techniques, and that Western-blot and one and two dimensional gels are useful tools to identify the target antigens recognized by AMA.
ELISA is a promising screening test for the detection of type M2 anti-mitochondria antibodies in primary biliary cirhosis, but some false positive results are observed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the detection of M2 AMA in PBC sera, and the identification of M2 target polypeptides.
the development of an ELISA technique for the screening and the identification of the M2 target antigems.
the use of ELISA for the screening of AMA in the diagnosis of PBC and the use of Western-blot and two-dimensional gel techniques for identifying the polypeptides which are recognized by M2 AMA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

(1), ELISA is a sensitive and rapid method to detect AMA in PBC. (2), Western-blot techniques can identify some of the M2 AMA target antigens, but the sensitivity is lower than that of IF. (3), The identification of AMA target antigens by two-dimensional gel electro-phoresis is a promising approach to identify AMA target antigens.
ELISA is the most sensitive method, but it should be used with a double confirmation by IF or CFT.
ELISA is a very useful screening method, but the final diagnosis of PBC must be confirmed by other techniques.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ELISA is a promising method for screening type M2 AMA, although it is still necessary to confirm positive results by another technique.
the Western-blot technique is a useful tool for the identification of M2 AMA and that ELISA is a sensitive screening method.

ELISA, though a promising method, should be used in combination with other tests for the detection of AMA, and Western-blot and one- and two-dimensional electrophoresis should be used in the identification of M2 antigens.

the ELISA technique is a promising screening method for the detection of AMA in PBC.
